comment: Fault 8 of a Windows session replayed with embedded subwindows off, so every docker is a window of its own as it is on Windows. The sequence under WinTab: Colour Picker dragged by its title by (-400, 200), summoned from the far side with Alt+Shift+C and left until it went back, then Tool Options (Alt+Shift+D, Alt+Shift+O at the time), Reference (Alt+Shift+F), Recorder (Alt+Shift+X, Alt+Shift+R at the time) and a locked Layers (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+T) summoned in turn, each left past the dwell, and Layers, held by its lock past the dwell, sent back by its chord pressed twice within the second, since the lock button's name is one of thirteen and the click would find the toolbox's. On Windows Colour Picker ended as a picture the OS listed as hidden. Here the state after each step says whether the window is visible and where, and the last drag says whether it still moves by its title.

The faults 12 and 13: a Windows session pressed the Colour Picker's summon, Alt+Shift with its letter, with the pointer still on Colour Picker's title and Colour Picker in front, and that made the ghost. Here the pointer is put on its title where the drag left it and the chord is pressed, and the state says whether the docker is shown and where. Wayland gives no client the keyboard it asks for, so the docker does not hold the keyboard as it did on Windows, and a suite of its own holds that half.
